title.value: UNDERSTANDING ZERO-SHOT ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS FOR LARGE-SCALE MODELS
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the main focus of the paper, which is on exploring zero-shot adversarial robustness in large-scale models like CLIP.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023

U NDERSTANDING Z ERO - SHOT A DVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS FOR L ARGE -S CALE M ODELS Chengzhi Mao1∗ Scott Geng1∗ Junfeng Yang1 Columbia University1 , Microsoft Research2

extractions.description: This paper explores the zero-shot adversarial robustness of large-scale vision-language models like CLIP. It identifies key factors affecting zero-shot adversarial robustness, such as training losses and adaptation methods. The work proposes a text-guided contrastive adversarial training loss that improves the alignment between text embeddings and adversarial visual features using contrastive learning. Through experiments, the study finds that visual prompt tuning without text is effective, while finetuning performs better with text guidance. The proposed approach significantly enhances zero-shot adversarial robustness over CLIP across several datasets.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper focuses on improving the robustness of vision-language models, which are important for various applications, it does not explicitly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as its central theme. The primary focus is on enhancing machine learning models' robustness in adversarial scenarios.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we identify and explore the problem of adapting large-scale models for zero-shot adversarial robustness.
